clue.text: It's unusual, Marilyn, but not unknown — have it out

definitions.note: It is short for 'Italian', as in a gin and It

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are arranged in a new way
but not says one thing is excluded, so a letter is dropped from the name Marilyn

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Someone tells Marilyn that her behaviour is odd but no surprise, and that they should argue it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'It' and the 's is a link meaning 'is'. MARILN (Marilyn less Y) and HAVEITOUT are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: In a gin and It, the It is a sweet red vermouth from Italy, so 'It' is a familiar short name for that drink.

clue.text: Making unwelcome contact with maidens in country — over a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
in says the maidens sit inside the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a country
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so two maidens give MM
G stands for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone pesters young women in a foreign country, more than a thousand of them.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spamming means sending unsolicited messages in bulk, an unwanted kind of contact.

clue.text: Good to have nude round boat

indicators.note: round says the word for nude goes around the letter for good

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: Someone recommends going naked around a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: One in speech covers list of offences

indicators.note: in says the letter for one sits inside the speech abbreviation

parts.note: RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard accent of British speech
A means one, as in a single thing
to sheet something is to cover it, as with a sheet

explanation.surface: Someone gives a talk covering a list of crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the prestige accent of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is a police record listing someone's past convictions.

clue.text: Has to keep very quiet about love poet

indicators.note: about says the combination is turned round
to keep says the word has holds the letters for very quiet inside it

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, the musical mark for very quiet
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone must stay hushed about a poet of love.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS holding PP gives HPPAS, which turned 'about' gives SAPPH. 'Love poet' looks like the definition, but love supplies O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the ancient Greek lyric writer from Lesbos, famous for verse.

clue.text: Seeing and disapproving of son getting engaged

indicators.note: getting engaged is read as being taken in, so the son sits inside the other word

parts.note: decrying means disapproving of

explanation.surface: A parent spots and frowns at their son getting engaged to be married.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of something, so descrying means spotting or seeing.

clue.text: Aunt suffering with health — it's an old scourge

indicators.note: suffering suggests something damaged, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An aunt's poor health is called a plague from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of it's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century leader of the Huns was called the Scourge of God for ravaging Europe.

clue.text: Chaotic — a bit reminiscent of Grayling, perhaps

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is muddled, rather like the fish called the grayling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grayling' looks like the fish; it is Chris Grayling, a UK Conservative politician who held several senior government posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Grayling sat in the British Cabinet, an example of a senior government member.

clue.text: Most important person to lead America? Idiot!

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
nana is British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the leader of America is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The top banana is slang for the boss, the chief figure in an organisation.

clue.text: More from Turkey's premier artist

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letter of Turkey is taken

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Something more comes from Turkey's leading painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, an added amount beyond the usual.

clue.text: Car journeys taking off round French city

parts.note: a limo is a luxury car

indicators.note: taking off says a letter is removed from the word for journeys

parts.note: goes means journeys, as a verb
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Trips by limousine set off around a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, known for porcelain.

clue.text: Composer Henry ignored minor problem over National Insurance

indicators.note: over says the remaining letters are turned round
ignored says the letter for Henry is left out

parts.note: a hiccup is a small setback
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
NI is National Insurance, the UK social security contribution

explanation.surface: A composer called Henry shrugged off a slight snag with his tax contributions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like the composer's first name; it gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian who wrote the operas La Bohème and Tosca.

clue.text: Nothing is held back? Don't believe it!

indicators.note: back says the result reads in reverse
held says the word is sits within the letters for nothing

parts.note: FA is Fanny Adams, as in 'sweet FA', meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Someone asks if nothing has been kept back, and gets scornful disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: F-IS-A reads backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As if! is an exclamation of disbelief or scorn.

clue.text: Way back

parts.note: a long time ago, read also as a route leading backwards into the past

explanation.surface: Simply a long time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a trip down this lane means reminiscing, a road into one's past.

clue.text: How to sell admirer snaps — look inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for look goes into the jumbled letters
snaps means breaks, so the letters of admirer are broken up

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An admirer takes photos and sells them, inviting someone to look inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is a way of retailing goods by post from a catalogue.

clue.text: Opposed to some financial help for drifter

parts.note: V is versus, meaning against
a means some, an unspecified one
a grant is money given as aid

explanation.surface: Someone objects to giving any welfare money to a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a homeless wanderer with no settled home.

clue.text: Retreat from problem — can new Head of Technology crack it?

indicators.note: crack means break into, so the letters go inside the word for problem

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form of the word can
head of takes the first letter of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a tricky problem, wondering if a new tech chief can solve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' reads as a trouble to flee, but it is an arithmetic exercise; 'new' rearranges can, 'Head of' takes one letter, and 'crack' breaks into the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room or refuge where one withdraws undisturbed.

clue.text: 'I'm clueless!' — Hunt to Amber regularly

parts.note: to search is to hunt

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Amber

explanation.surface: A cluelessness complaint passed from someone called Hunt to someone called Amber.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt and Amber look like names (Jeremy Hunt, Amber Rudd, both Conservative ministers); Hunt is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an idiom meaning I have no idea.

clue.text: One's lucky having time with Angelo Dundee?

parts.note: Angelo Dundee was the trainer of the boxer Muhammad Ali, so he was Ali's man

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they're fortunate to be spending time with a famous boxing trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Angelo Dundee as a definition by example: he was Ali's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm believed to bring good fortune, a lucky object.

clue.text: Knackered old bus conductor's role reversal

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

indicators.note: reversal says the word for role is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A bus conductor swaps jobs, perhaps with the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' looks like the bus worker; it is the orchestral conductor Simon Rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety old vehicle that shakes and rattles.

clue.text: See 7
'Second-rate!' Upset about new book collection

indicators.note: about says the word for upset goes round the letter for new

parts.note: to tip is to upset, as in tip over
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a new book collection as inferior and is annoyed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something cheap and inferior, of poor quality.

clue.text: Idea to reduce growth

indicators.note: to reduce says the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: a plant is a growing thing

explanation.surface: Someone has a scheme for cutting back growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or intention, a worked-out notion.

clue.text: Approval for one like this

parts.note: say means for example, as does for one
so means in this way

explanation.surface: Someone seeks endorsement for a person of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so means permission or authorisation given by someone with authority.

clue.text: Somewhat perverse — lunar revolution took longer than expected

indicators.note: perverse means contrary, so the run of letters is read the wrong way
somewhat says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A moon's orbit took a bit longer than planned, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards inside 'lunar revolution'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go on beyond the allotted time, as a meeting might.

clue.text: Over 50 reasons they might be dependent

indicators.note: over says the word for reasons sits over, covering, the Roman numeral

parts.note: causes are reasons
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Over fifty motives which might rely on something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Grammar has dependent (subordinate) clauses that cannot stand alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a subordinate sentence part is called dependent, relying on a main one.

clue.text: On return, initially enjoyed short break from action

indicators.note: on return says the word for short is read backwards

parts.note: curt means short in manner

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of enjoyed

explanation.surface: After coming back, someone had a brief enjoyable rest from fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a pause in fighting agreed by both sides, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Shambles a government covered up by individual speaking thus

definitions.note: describes speaking in line with the agreed party message

indicators.note: covered up by says the following pieces sit inside the word for individual

parts.note: one means a single individual
a shambles is a mess

explanation.surface: An individual hides a government mess, speaking in the approved way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue pictures a loyal spokesperson concealing the shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who keeps to the official party line is described with this phrase, sticking to agreed talking points.
